states.content: Elena Morales is the kidney-lupus patient. She is here for an urgent rheumatology follow-up for swelling, foamy urine, and concern for a lupus kidney flare. Her primary team requested a same-day review because her legs are swelling again and her urine looks foamy. She reports two weeks of ankle swelling, darker foamy urine, fatigue, and more joint pain, as recorded in the intake summary. Symptom callback note: swelling is a little better and there is no dizziness. Latest symptom update: swelling is down a little and urine looks less foamy today. Triage callback: no dizziness and urine output is okay. Dr. Lin is treating this as a likely lupus nephritis flare until testing and nephrology review are complete. Dr. Lin's plan is prednisone 40 mg daily, urine protein plus CBC/CMP/C3/C4 today, and a nephrology visit next week. Medication counseling recap: start prednisone 40 mg daily, keep hydroxychloroquine 200 mg twice daily, and stop ibuprofen. Short lab recap right now: creatinine 1.6, urine protein/creatinine 1.9, and C3 low. CMP follow-up posted: potassium 4.6 and the rest of the CMP is stable.
